newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-Indian GDRs edge up in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-Indian GDRs edge up in slow trade.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts ended little changed on Thursday as prices continued to consolidate after volatility related to the country's political crisis.
Traders said prices were steady but volumes limited as the market scratched for direction amid little fresh news.
Stocks in India drifted easier, but were off lows by the close on news that former finance minister P. Chidambaram's party may rejoin the government.
Dealers said GDRs could post gains on Friday if local stocks extended their climb off lows.
They said GDR prices continued to be capped by relatively high premiums to the local market, and were unlikely to show much upside without a strong showing from local stocks.
Reliance added 77 cents to $18.90/$19.90, SBI made 56 cents to $24.25/$25.25 and VSNL lost 20 cents to $19.40/19.90.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI closed 0.11 points, or 0.14 percent, up at 80.07, with the premium over the local market at 19.98 percent from 18.88 percent.
The Bombay Stock Exchange 30 share index shed 23.27 points to 3,805.72.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index added 0.63 points to 129.43, representing a discount to the local market of 1.87 percent.
The Capel Korea GDR Index ended 0.08 points, or 0.13 percent, up at 64.13, a premium of 34.21 percent over the local market.
